source.collection_label: Tim Kirk · Oxford 2003 · 1998 question reproductions

parts.label: a
parts.display_text: A car approaches a stationary observer while sounding a 660 Hz horn. Explain, using a wavefront sketch, why the observer hears a higher frequency.

answer.text: Draw successive circular wavefronts centred on successive car positions. They are closer together ahead of the car, so the stationary observer receives more wavefronts each second.

parts.label: e
parts.display_text: Andromeda approaches Earth at 100 km s⁻¹. A spectral line is emitted at 500 nm. Estimate the observed wavelength using the low-speed Doppler approximation.

answer.text: Δλ/λ ≈ −v/c, so λobserved ≈ 500(1 − 1.0 × 10⁵/3.0 × 10⁸) = 499.83 nm. It is a blueshift.

parts.label: a.i
parts.display_text: A spectral line has wavelength 434 nm for a stationary source and is observed at 502 nm from a receding astronomical source. State whether this is a redshift or a blueshift, and what the shift indicates about radial motion.

answer.text: It is a redshift: the observed wavelength is longer. In the Doppler interpretation, the source is receding from the observer.

notes: For sound, source motion changes the spacing of wavefronts; observer motion changes how quickly they are encountered. Choose the Doppler signs so approach increases observed frequency.
For collinear motion, f_obs = f_source(v ± v_observer)/(v ∓ v_source), with speeds measured relative to the medium. Do not simply exchange source and observer speeds.

sup-5e62e7fd42677f6d-q23:whole.hint: Compare the observed wavelength with the laboratory wavelength before calculating the speed.
notes: For radial speeds much smaller than c, Δλ/λ₀ ≈ v_r/c. Use the rest wavelength λ₀ in the denominator.

notes: Use v = fλ and f = 1/T. A spatial separation between equal-phase points gives wavelength; a time separation gives period.

notes: For initially in-phase sources, constructive interference has path difference nλ; destructive interference has (n + ½)λ.
For a double slit at small angles, fringe spacing is λD/d. Use slit separation d, not slit width, and distinguish adjacent-fringe spacing from distance to a particular order.

ibd-156cd4cef22f7d6e-q5:c.hint: Compare wave speeds on the two sides and draw a normal at the boundary.
notes: A wave entering a slower medium bends towards the normal; entering a faster medium bends away. Frequency stays fixed, so wavelength changes in proportion to speed.
Wavefronts are perpendicular to rays. For parallel faces returning to the original medium, the emerging ray is parallel to the incident ray but can be displaced sideways.
